questions.stem: What do we learn about David Jackson from the conversation?
questions.stemZh: 从对话中我们了解到关于David Jackson的什么信息?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Mr. David Jackson, a staff writer at the New Yorker, is known for his non-fiction books of adventure. David Jackson 先生，《纽约客》的专职撰稿人，以其纪实类冒险题材的书而闻名。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 开场介绍句直接报身份。主持人开场第一句就用同位语把人物头衔报全：a staff writer at the New Yorker。人物介绍题的答案信号就是这种"姓名 + 同位语头衔"的引入句，听到立 刻锁定。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: a staff writer at the New Yorker ↔He is a staff writer. 原句同位语 选项主系表，几乎原词对应

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 原词陷阱 原文说他 is known for his non-fiction books of adventure——写冒险题材的书，是"写 冒险的人"不是"亲历冒险的人"。He is an adventurer. 盗用 adventure 一词，把"写冒险 书"偷换成"他本人是冒险家"，听到 adventure 就选会中招。 借用原文：is known for his non-fiction books of adventure C) 与原文相反 原文明确是 non-fiction books（纪实/非虚构），He is an author of fiction. 却说他写 fiction（虚构小说），正好把 non-fiction 的 non 抹掉、极性反了。听到 fiction 这半个原 词就选，等于没听清前面的否定前缀。 借用原文：non-fiction books of adventure D) 未提及 原文只说他有 an 11- and a 14-year-old（一个 11 岁、一个 14 岁，共两个孩子），He is a father of four kids. 凭空说"四个孩子"。four 这个数字原文从未出现，是偷改数字的陷 阱。

options.label: C
options.text: He is an author of fiction.

options.label: D
options.text: He is a father of four kids.

questions.stem: What does the man think of young teenagers?
questions.stemZh: 男士对年轻青少年有什么看法?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: They are independent, and they have their own curiosities and obsessions. 他们很独立，有自己的好奇心和着迷的东西。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者的正面评价应答。女方问他这阶段孩子的情况，男方应答先说 I find these ages to be kind of wonderful，再具体说 They are independent, and they have their own curiosities。对话题答案落在被问者的应答里，wonderful 与 independent、curiosities 是定调的正面信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: They are independent ↔They are curious and autonomous. independent=autonomous 同义替换 their own curiosities ↔curious 名词 curiosities 形容词 curious 词形转换

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 原文说能和孩子聊 sophisticated subject matter such as politics，即谈"成熟话题如政 治"，反衬他们不幼稚；They are interested in fairy tales. 童话与原文要表达的"能聊成熟 话题"恰恰相反，且 fairy tales 原文根本没提，是借"孩子"语境硬造的话题。 借用原文：sophisticated subject matter such as politics C) 与原文相反 男方明明说 I find these ages to be kind of wonderful（觉得这年纪很好），They are a headache to their parents. 却说孩子让父母头疼，与他的正面评价完全相反。这是把褒义 答案反向设成贬义的陷阱。 借用原文：I find these ages to be kind of wonderful D) 原词陷阱 原文说能和孩子聊 politics，恰恰说明他们"懂/能聊政治"；They are ignorant of politics. 盗用 politics 原词，却说他们"对政治无知"，意思正好反过来。听到 politics 就选会直接掉 坑。 借用原文：such as politics

options.label: A
options.text: They are interested in fairy tales.
options.textZh: 他们对童话故事感兴趣。

options.label: B
options.textZh: 他们好奇且自主。

options.label: C
options.text: They are a headache to their parents.
options.textZh: 他们让父母头疼。

options.label: D
options.textZh: 他们对政治一无所知。

questions.stem: How does the man help his kids with their essays?
questions.stemZh: 男士如何帮助他的孩子们写作文?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I really just try to be encouraging. I think at this age, editorial guidance is less important than encouragement. 我真的只是尽量给予鼓励。我觉得在这个年纪，编辑式的指导不如鼓励来得重要。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 取舍句 less important than 落在后半。男方先表态 I really just try to be encouraging，再用取舍句 editorial guidance is less important than encouragement。"A is less important than B" 的信号是：被贬低的 A（指导）是陪衬， 强调的 B（鼓励）才是答案。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I really just try to be encouraging ↔He gives them encouragement. be encouraging→give encouragement 形容词转名词

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 选项 He offers them ample editorial guidance. 盗用原文 editorial guidance 原词，可 原文恰恰说它 less important than encouragement——他不强调指导。听到 editorial guidance 就选，正好掉进"被贬低项"的坑，且 ample（大量）更与他"只是尽量鼓励"的克 制相反。 借用原文：editorial guidance is less important than encouragement B) 未提及 He recommends model essays to them. 借了 essays 这个语境词（女方确实问到 proofread their essays），但"推荐范文（model essays）"这件事男方从没说过，是凭"帮 写作"语境硬造的做法。 D) 张冠李戴 proofread 这个词确实出现，但它出自女方提问 Do they ask you to proofread their essays?，是"孩子请他校对"，并非"他教孩子校对"。He teaches them proofreading. 把 女方问句里的词搬来、又改成"他教校对"，既盗原词又错了施动方。 借用原文：Do they ask you to proofread their essays?

options.label: A
options.text: He offers them ample editorial guidance.
options.textZh: 他为他们提供充分的编辑指导。

options.label: B
options.text: He recommends model essays to them.
options.textZh: 他向他们推荐范文。

options.label: C
options.textZh: 他给予他们鼓励。

options.label: D
options.textZh: 他教他们校对。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about herself when she was a teenager?
questions.stemZh: 女士说她十几岁时是什么情况?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I feel that children's tastes in books change as they reach adolescence. I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager. 我觉得孩子的读书口味会随着进入青春期而改变。我知道我自己当年读中学时口味确实 变了。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: mine + when I was a teenager 锁定她谈自己。女方说 I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager，mine 回指 tastes in books，when I was a teenager 正对题干 限定。第一人称 mine/I 加"少年时"，是"她说自己"的答案信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: children's tastes in books change ↔Her tastes in books changed. mine did 还原为 her tastes changed

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 张冠李戴 She realized the power of reading. 里的 power 出自男方 they give you the power to begin to perceive the world，是男方谈读书的话，不是女方说自己；且女方从没说她"意 识到读书的力量"。既错主语又属未提及。 借用原文：they give you the power to begin to perceive the world C) 张冠李戴 Her reading opened her eyes to the world. 盗用男方 read subject matter that'll open their eyes to the world 的原词 open eyes to the world，但这是男方对"孩子该读什么"的 看法，主语既不是"她"、内容也非她自述。听到 open eyes 就选会被男方的话误导。 借用原文：open their eyes to the world D) 原词陷阱 She began to perceive the world differently. 盗用男方 to perceive the world through the lives of others 的 perceive the world，但这同样是男方对读书意义的论述，非女方谈 自己。与 C 是一对孪生干扰，靠"主语是谁"才能切开。 借用原文：perceive the world through the lives of others 1 M: In this episode of Money Talks, our guest is Molly Sanders, a university student and a successful young entrepreneur. Molly, tell us about your business. M: 在本期《金钱对话》节目中,我们的嘉宾是 Molly Sanders,一位大学生,也是一位成功的年轻企业家。 Molly,跟我们说说你的生意吧。 2 W: Well, I sell specialty clothes through a website, mainly for women who have trouble finding suitable clothes in main street shops because of their height or weight. But I do some men's clothes too. W: 嗯,我通过网站销售特殊服装,主要面向那些因为身高或体重在主流商店很难找到合适衣服的女性。不过 我也做一些男装。 3 M: How did you get started in this business at such a young age? Are you studying fashion design? M: 你这么年轻是怎么开始做这个生意的?你学的是时装设计吗? 4 W: Actually, I'm majoring in finance, but I've always loved clothes. And I started making my own at 14. W: 其实我主修的是金融,但我一直很喜欢服装。我14岁就开始自己做衣服了。 5 M: Did you have any sort of training in design or sewing? Or was it a natural ability? M: 你接受过设计或缝纫方面的培训吗?还是说这是天生的能力? Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 6 W: I'd have to say no to both. No one taught me to make clothes and most of the things I made at first were disasters. W: 我得说两个都不是。没人教过我做衣服,而且我最开始做的东西大多都很糟糕。 7 M: Why did you persevere? I think most people would give up if they kept failing, especially at that age. M: 那你为什么还坚持下来?我觉得大多数人如果一直失败就会放弃,尤其是在那个年纪。 8 W: I kept on out of necessity. As you can see, I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops. So I kept trying and developed my skills over time. W: 我坚持下来是出于需要。你看得出来,我个子很高,在普通商店里找不到合身的衣服。所以我就不断尝试, 慢慢提高了技能。 9 M: Well, my notes say you earned $50,000 in profits last year, an extraordinary amount for a 20-year- old student. How did that happen? Did you see a gap in the market and decide to fill it? M: 嗯,我的资料上说你去年赚了5万美元利润,对一个20岁的学生来说是个惊人的数字。这是怎么做到的?你 是发现了市场空缺然后决定填补它吗? 10 W: No. When I started university, some classmates complimented my clothes. And when I said I made them myself, other tall women started asking if I would make theirs. And I did. And before I knew it, I was an entrepreneur. W: 不是。我上大学的时候,有些同学夸我的衣服好看。当我说是自己做的时候,其他高个子女生就开始问我 能不能给她们做。我就做了。然后不知不觉中,我就成了企业家。 11 M: So what are your plans for the future? Do you intend to open a physical store? M: 那你未来有什么计划?打算开实体店吗? 12 W: No. I'll keep things online to keep costs down. But I will add more clothes for children, both girls and boys, and possibly even for infants. And I hope to add to my range of designs for men. W: 不打算。我会继续做线上生意来控制成本。但我会增加更多儿童服装,包括女孩和男孩的,可能还有婴儿 装。我还希望扩大男装的设计种类。

options.label: A
options.textZh: 她对书籍的品味发生了变化。

options.label: B
options.text: She realized the power of reading.
options.textZh: 她意识到了阅读的力量。

options.label: C
options.text: Her reading opened her eyes to the world.
options.textZh: 她的阅读让她开阔了眼界。

options.label: D
options.text: She began to perceive the world differently.
options.textZh: 她开始以不同的方式感知世界。

questions.stemZh: 关于这位女士我们了解到什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: In this episode of Money Talks, our guest is Molly Sanders, a university student and a successful young entrepreneur. 在本期《财富对话》中，我们的嘉宾是莫莉·桑德斯，一名大学生，也是一位成功的年轻创 业者。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 主持人开场介绍嘉宾的同位语。答案信号是开场白里介绍嘉宾身份的同位语 a university student and a successful young entrepreneur——访谈类听力里，嘉宾身份几乎都在主 持人开场这句 our guest is… 后面交代。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: a successful young entrepreneur ↔She is a successful entrepreneur. 近乎同词，只省去 young

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 原词陷阱 录音确实说她是 a university student，She is a university graduate. 借此设套；但一来 题问我们了解到什么，主持人重点捧的是 successful entrepreneur，二来 student（在 读）不等于 graduate（已毕业），身份还被偷改了。 借用原文：a university student A) 过度推断 后文她说 I sell specialty clothes through a website，但用网站卖衣服不等于她是做网站 的设计师，She is a website designer. 是从 website 一词过度联想出来的。 借用原文：I sell specialty clothes through a website C) 与原文相反 她明确说将来 I'll keep things online to keep costs down，根本不开实体店，She is a main street store owner. 与原文相反；main street 还是她顾客买不到衣服的地方，并非 她开店之处。 借用原文：I'll keep things online to keep costs down

questions.stem: What does the woman say about the clothes she made at first?
questions.stemZh: 关于她最初制作的衣服,这位女士说了什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: No one taught me to make clothes and most of the things I made at first were disasters. 没人教过我做衣服，而且我最初做的大多数东西都是惨不忍睹的失败品。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者直接应答里的自我评价词。主持人问她是否有天赋，她应答中的 most of the things I made at first were disasters 是直接评价句，disasters 这个强贬义词就是答案信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: were disasters ↔They were mostly failures. disasters 约等于 failures 的同义替换

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: C) 原词陷阱 主持人问 Or was it a natural ability?，They showed her natural talent. 盗用了 natural 一词；但她明确回答 I'd have to say no to both（天赋、培训都没有），所以显出天赋恰 与原文相反。 借用原文：Or was it a natural ability? A) 未提及 They were repeatedly rejected by shops. 听着像创业故事，但录音从没说她最初的衣服 被商店反复拒收；她说的是顾客在 main street shops 买不到合身的，张冠李戴了。 B) 张冠李戴 同学称赞她衣服确有其事——some classmates complimented my clothes，They were popular with her classmates. 借此设套；但那是她上大学后的事，不是最初（14岁）做 的，时间错位。 借用原文：some classmates complimented my clothes

questions.stem: Why did the woman persevere in making clothes for herself?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士为什么坚持为自己制作衣服?
questions.answerText: She could not find clothes of her size.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I kept on out of necessity. As you can see, I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops. 我是出于无奈才坚持下来的。如你所见，我个子很高，在普通商店里找不到合身的衣服。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 原因短语 out of necessity 引出理由。答案信号是因果短语 out of necessity（出于必 需），其后紧跟的 I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me 就是真正原因。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops ↔She could not find clothes of her size. fit me 约等于 of her size 的同义改写

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 答非所问 她确说过 I've always loved clothes，She had a strong interest in doing it. 借喜爱设 套；但那解释的是她为何开始做衣服，题问的是为何坚持，她坚持的理由是无奈，不是兴 趣。 借用原文：I've always loved clothes D) 未提及 She found clothes in shops unaffordable. 与C都涉及商店的衣服，迷惑性强；但录音说 的是找不到合身的，从未提到买不起、太贵，价格问题纯属杜撰。 B) 未提及 She did not like ready-made clothes. 听着合理，但录音只说商店里没有合她身的，从没 说她不喜欢现成衣服；她做衣服是因买不到，不是因厌恶成衣。

questions.stem: What does the woman plan to do in the future?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士将来打算做什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: But I will add more clothes for children, both girls and boys, and possibly even for infants. And I hope to add to my range of designs for men. 不过我会增加儿童服装，男孩女孩都做，可能还会做婴幼儿的。我也希望扩充我给男士设计 的产品线。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 将来意图信号 I will 与 I hope to。答案信号是 I will add more clothes for children 与 I hope to add to my range of designs for men 里的 will、hope to——它们标志将来计 划，后接的增加品类即答案。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: add more clothes for children ↔Expand her business. 具体加品类等于概括的扩展生意

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: C) 偷换概念 她确说 add to my range of designs for men，Add designs for women. 却把对象由 men（男士）偷换成 women（女士），方向都改错了，且她加的远不止男装。 借用原文：add to my range of designs for men A) 原词陷阱 前文主持人问 Are you studying fashion design?，Study fashion design at college. 盗 用了 fashion design；但她回答 I'm majoring in finance，学的是金融，更没把学时装设 计当未来计划。 借用原文：Are you studying fashion design? B) 未提及 Improve her marketing strategy. 听着像生意人会做的事，但录音谈未来时只说加品类、 保持线上控成本，从没提改进营销策略。 Section B 1 Researchers have identified a potent new antibiotic compound using artificial intelligence. The antibiotic can kill very dangerous bacteria. According to a study published in the journal Cell, the compound successfully removed deadly strains of bacteria in mice which are resistant to all known antibiotics. 研究人员利用人工智能识别出一种强效的新型抗生素化合物。该抗生素可以杀死非常危险的细菌。根据发 表在《细胞》杂志上的一项研究,该化合物成功清除了小鼠体内对所有已知抗生素都具有耐药性的致命细菌 菌株。 2 The researchers say this is the first time that artificial intelligence has been used to find a powerful new antibiotic molecule. Why does this matter? The answer is antibiotic resistance. This happens when bacteria develop the ability to survive the medications designed to kill them. Antibiotic resistance is a serious threat to health and the problem is growing. This makes finding new antibiotics very important. However, in recent decades, very few have been developed, and those that have tend to be very similar to drugs already available. The searches also tend to only focus on a narrow spectrum of chemical compounds, but this is where artificial intelligence comes in. Why? To find new drugs, scientists screen molecules to predict how effective they might be. Typically, such screening is done by humans in the lab, which is both costly and slow. Artificial intelligence is different. It's fast, and it can process a high volume. It can screen hundreds of millions of compounds to identify a few interesting candidates that require experimental testing. Patients are incidental." 「如果你说一句负面的话,他们就会变得防御,」她后来告诉我。「他们有这种机构忠诚度。一定要带一个 代言人,也就是任何其他人和你一起去医院,并写下每一个问题和答案,每一位医生和护士的名字。当人们知 道你记下了他们的名字,他们会表现得更好。而且,」Brudney补充道,「如果你作为患者暗示你可能想控制 哪怕一部分情况,或者被咨询或告知,那么你就会被认为很难相处。他们希望你完全被动。整个医疗保健系 统,特别是医院和疗养院,存在的理由与照顾患者无关。患者只是附带的。」

When people know you have their names, they behave better. 一定要带一个能为你说话的人，也就是任何别的人，陪你去医院，并且把每一个问题和答 案、每一位医生和护士的名字都写下来。当别人知道你掌握着他们的名字时，他们就会表现 得更好。

questions.stem: What do American doctors expect their patients to be, according to Karen Brudney?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: They want you to be totally passive. 他们想要你完全被动顺从。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: want 表期望 + totally 强调。答案句以 They want you to be totally passive 直白给出期 望：want 正对题干 expect，totally 加重语气强调这正是医院想要的状态，是明确的答案 落点。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: They want you to be totally passive ↔Passive. 原词直现：passive=Passive

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 偷换概念 Cooperative. 听感上像『听话配合』，与 passive 沾边，易误选。但原文用的是 passive （被动顺从），强调的是『别插手、别要求』，而非主动『配合』；cooperative 是录音没 有的词。 B) 原词陷阱 Appreciative.（感激的）与开篇 grateful 含义呼应，易让听过 grateful 的人误选。但本题 问的是答案句 They want you to be totally passive 给出的特质，是 passive 不是感激； appreciative 并非此句所述。 借用原文：grateful D) 与原文相反 Responsive.（主动回应的）正是 Passive 的反义。原文明说医院要病人 totally passive （完全被动），responsive 取了相反方向；它恰恰是病人想被知情、被咨询那种主动姿 态，而那会被医院当成难缠。 借用原文：They want you to be totally passive 1 There are probably teams you've worked with but you never want to work with again. But there must have also been other teams that you would prize reuniting with professionally. In other words, your team had vitality. Vitality comes about when the ties people form with their fellow team members are such that they stay connected even after the team breaks up. 可能有些团队你曾与之共事但再也不想合作。但也一定有其他团队,你会珍视能在职业上重聚的机会。换句 话说,你的团队具有活力。活力产生于团队成员之间形成的纽带,这种纽带使他们即使在团队解散后仍保持 联系。 2 What characteristics of a team make its members more likely to stay in contact despite no longer working together? This question has been answered recently in a study published in a business journal. 是什么团队特征使其成员更有可能在不再共事后仍保持联系?这个问题最近在一份商业期刊发表的研究中 得到了解答。 3 One of the two key factors the research team discovered is sameness. Specifically, sharing the same gender or ethnic origin. The more members of a team share similar demographics, the more inclined they Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard. will be to remain associates long after the team has served its purpose. After ties are established, similarity strengthens them. As a result, they regard these individuals with greater trust and mutual understanding, which motivates them to seek further opportunities for collaboration. In effect, people tend to create stronger and longer-lasting connections with similar others. Someone who looks and sounds different from us may have the resources we need to be more successful. Yet, we find them to be significantly less credible simply because they are different. If you are a fierce advocate of workplace diversity, you'll no doubt be horrified by such a revelation. 研究团队发现的两个关键因素之一是相似性。具体来说,是共享相同的性别或种族血统。团队成员之间人口 统计学特征越相似,他们在团队完成使命后仍保持联系的可能性就越大。在建立联系之后,相似性会强化这 些联系。因此,他们对这些人抱有更大的信任和相互理解,这促使他们寻求进一步合作的机会。实际上,人们 倾向于与相似的人建立更牢固、更持久的联系。一个外表和声音都与我们不同的人可能拥有我们取得更大 成功所需的资源。然而,我们发现他们的可信度明显较低,仅仅因为他们不同。如果你是职场多元化的坚定 倡导者,毫无疑问你会对这样的发现感到震惊。 4 The second factor identified by the researchers is the quality of the relationships among the team members. The more they trust one another, share the same goals and depend on each other for the achievement of those goals, the stronger their chances of maintaining their connections, despite no longer working as one team. Teams with quality relationships have a shared belief that it's safe to take risks with each other, and their members are obliged to share the workload and help out. 研究人员确定的第二个因素是团队成员之间关系的质量。他们彼此越信任,越能共享相同目标,越依赖彼此 来实现这些目标,他们维持联系的可能性就越大,尽管不再作为一个团队工作。拥有高质量关系的团队有一 个共同信念,即与彼此冒险是安全的,他们的成员有义务分担工作量并互相帮助。 5 From personal experience, I can see both the truth and the inconsistency of such studies. The truth is some of my closest friendships were formed as a result of having worked together on teams, and I actively seek opportunities to work with them again. The inconsistency, though, is that I've never worked for a team more successful and cohesive than the one of which I am a member right now. And yet, the four of us have very little in common and are completely different demographically. So I am unlikely to question the value of a diverse workforce. 从个人经验来看,我能看到此类研究的真实性和不一致性。真实性在于,我的一些最亲密的友谊是通过在团 队中共事而形成的,我积极寻求与他们再次合作的机会。然而,不一致之处在于,我从未在一个比我现在所在 的团队更成功、更有凝聚力的团队中工作过。然而,我们四个人几乎没有共同点,在人口统计学上完全不 同。因此,我不太可能质疑多元化员工队伍的价值。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: And yet, the four of us have very little in common and are completely different demographically. 然而，我们四个人几乎没有共同点，在人口特征上完全不同。

analysis.label: 信号

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: have very little in common and are completely different demographically ↔ characterized by diversity "几乎无共同点、完全不同" = diversity

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 原词陷阱 B 说团队 goals are quite inconsistent，借了录音 the inconsistency 一词，但那个 inconsistency 指的是"研究结论与说话者经历不一致"，不是说这支团队的目标不一致，原 词被挪错了对象。 借用原文：the inconsistency C) 与原文相反 C 称成员 have similar backgrounds，但录音明说当前团队 have very little in common、完全不同，C 取了相反极性，是被前文研究讲的"相似"带偏。 借用原文：have very little in common D) 未提及 D 说团队 connected by a unique mechanism，录音从未提任何"独特机制"，是凭"这么成 功一定有什么特别机制"想象出来的，原文无据。 1 An American researcher who studied 600 millionaires found how rich you can get comes down to six wealth factors. She found that six behaviors are related to net worth potential, regardless of age or income. These were thriftiness, confidence, responsibility, planning, focus and social indifference. 一位研究了600名百万富翁的美国研究人员发现,你能变得多富有取决于六个财富因素。她发现,无论年龄或 收入如何,有六种行为与净资产潜力相关。这些行为是节俭、自信、责任感、规划、专注和社交冷漠。 2 Being thrifty comes as no great surprise. Spending above your means, spending instead of saving for retirement, spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy, makes you a slave to the paycheck. "Even with an astronomical level of income," she wrote, "to properly build wealth, experts recommend saving 20% of your income and living off the remaining 80%." 节俭并不令人感到意外。入不敷出的消费、消费而不是为退休储蓄、因预期致富而消费,都会让你成为薪 水的奴隶。她写道:"即使收入达到天文数字,要想正确积累财富,专家建议储蓄收入的20%,靠剩余的80% 生活。" 3 Having confidence is another key characteristic, as it helps people to be thrifty. It takes confidence to live within your means. It also takes confidence to invest properly. Instead of making investing decisions Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard. with your emotions, financial planners advise that you should leave your investments alone and focus on a long-term investment plan. But people can't invest or manage their own money without accepting responsibility for the outcomes. Many millionaires take on personal responsibility, and most also happen to be self-made, meaning they didn't acquire their wealth through luck. Millionaires don't count on anyone else to make them rich, and they don't blame anyone else if they fall short. They focus on things they can control and align their daily habits to the goals they have set for themselves. They tend to be goal-oriented and hard workers, which enables them to plan financially and focus on seeing those plans through. 92% of the millionaires surveyed developed a long term plan for their money and 97% almost always achieved the goals they set for themselves. 拥有自信是另一个关键特征,因为它帮助人们保持节俭。量入为出需要自信,正确投资也需要自信。理财规 划师建议,与其用情绪做投资决策,不如让投资保持不动并专注于长期投资计划。但人们若不对结果承担责 任,就无法投资或管理自己的钱。许多百万富翁承担个人责任,而且大多数恰好是白手起家,这意味着他们不 是靠运气获得财富的。百万富翁不指望别人让他们致富,如果未能达成目标也不会责怪他人。他们专注于自 己能控制的事情,并使日常习惯与为自己设定的目标保持一致。他们往往以目标为导向且工作努力,这使他 们能够进行财务规划并专注于实现这些计划。在接受调查的百万富翁中,92%制定了长期理财计划,97%几 乎总是实现了为自己设定的目标。 4 And it is these behaviors that make it easy for them to be socially indifferent. They resist lifestyle creep, the tendency to spend more whenever one earns more. Essentially, they don't yield to pressure to buy the latest thing or to keep up with others or what they have acquired. Instead of being focused on what might make them happy today, they're focused on their long-term wealth-building plan. 正是这些行为使他们很容易保持社交冷漠。他们抵制生活方式攀升,即每当收入增加就消费更多的趋势。本 质上,他们不会屈服于购买最新物品或与他人攀比已获得之物的压力。他们不专注于今天什么能让他们快 乐,而是专注于长期财富积累计划。

P1 Selective colleges and universities in the U.S. are under fire for being too elite and too expensive, and for not training graduates for the world of work. Such charges ignore the fact that these institutions continue to prepare students for success in their work, for thoughtful engagement in civic life, for lifelong learning, and for understanding the world and those with whom they live.

P2 These colleges and universities must be doing something right. Applications are at record highs, and their financial aid programs make them more accessible than ever. This model of education has long played a central role in creating opportunity, driving economic growth, and spurring innovation.

P3 Yet, there is growing skepticism about the value of this model. The recent tax reform bill is a wake-up call that our strongest colleges and universities are under assault by some in government. The initial proposals would have made education unaffordable for many by taxing tuition waivers for graduate students and ending deductions for student loan interest. Thankfully, these provisions were Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage. ultimately stripped from the bill, but lawmakers let stand a new tax on the investment income of some colleges and universities.

P4 While these attacks are motivated by misguided ideas, we need to do a better job of explaining why these claims are false and why what we do is valuable. We cannot take for granted that any of this is obvious.

P5 It is often said that elite colleges and universities do not train students, particularly those who study the liberal arts, for the workforce. But this can be refuted by scholarly research. The data are clear: a liberal arts education is great career preparation, both for excellent lifetime earnings and for satisfaction with the work. This education develops the skills of critical thinking, rigorous analysis of data and facts, communication with the written and spoken word, understanding of cultural differences and issues, and the ability to keep learning. In fact, liberal arts graduates do extremely well in every imaginable field.

P6 Access to an education at selective colleges and universities is now more available than ever to low- and middle-income families. We have built endowments from donations by alumni( 校友) and parents who understand and appreciate our mission to provide access and opportunity, and a significant portion of the returns from these endowments is used to fund financial aid.

P7 Ironically, the new tax on endowments drains financial aid funds from the very schools most able to offer opportunity to those who have earned a spot but cannot otherwise afford this education. P2 But what do we mean by an appeal to common sense? Presumably it's an appeal to rationality of some sort that forms the basis of more complex reasoning. The appeal to common sense, however, is usually nothing more than an appeal to thinking that just feels right, but what feels right to one person may not feel right to another. Whether it feels right is usually a reflection of the world view and ideologies we have internalised, and that frames how we interact with new ideas. When new ideas are in accord with what we already believe, they are more readily accepted. When they are not, they, and the arguments that lead to them, are more readily rejected. P3 We often mistake this automatic compatibility testing of new ideas with existing beliefs as an application of common sense, but, in reality, it is more about judging than thinking. As Nobelist Daniel Kahneman notes in Thinking, Fast and Slow, when we arrive at conclusions in this way, the outcomes also feel true, regardless of whether they are. We are not psychologically well equipped to judge our own thinking.

P4 We are also highly susceptible to a range of cognitive biases such as giving preference to the first things that come to mind when making decisions or giving weight to evidence.

P5 One way we can check our internal biases and inconsistencies is through the social verification of knowledge, in which we test our ideas in a rigorous and systematic way to see if they make sense not just to us, but to other people. The outstanding example of this socially shared cognition is science.

P6 That does not mean that individuals are not capable of excellent thinking, nor does it mean no individual is rational. But the extent to which individuals can do this on their own is a function of how well integrated they are with communities of systematic inquiry in the first place. You can't learn to think well by yourself.

Lugou Bridge is not only world-famous for its aesthetic features but also widely recognized as a monument in the history of stone bridge construction.
translation.source: 卢沟桥位于天安门广场西南15公里处，横跨永定河，是北京现存最古老的多拱石桥。卢沟桥最初建成于1192年，1698年重建，由281根柱子支撑。每根柱子上都有一头石狮。这些石狮的头、背、腹部或爪子上都藏着更多的狮子。这些石狮生动逼真、千姿百态，是卢沟桥石刻艺术的精品。桥上的石狮不计其数，因而北京地区流传着"卢沟桥上的石狮子——数不清"的说法。 卢沟桥不仅以其美学特征闻名于世，还被公认为石桥建筑史上的一座丰碑。
translation.reference: Located 15 kilometres southwest of Tian'anmen Square and spanning the Yongding River, Lugou Bridge is the oldest existing multi-arch stone bridge in Beijing. It was first built in 1192 and rebuilt in 1698, and is supported by 281 pillars. On each pillar stands a stone lion, and on the heads, backs, bellies or paws of these stone lions are hidden even more lions. Vivid and lifelike and varying in posture, these stone lions are regarded as the finest works of stone carving on Lugou Bridge. The stone lions on the bridge are too numerous to count, so there is a popular saying in the Beijing area: "The stone lions on Lugou Bridge are simply countless." Lugou Bridge is not only world-famous for its aesthetic features but also widely recognized as a monument in the history of stone bridge construction.

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 卢沟桥 is 多拱石桥（主语策略：原句主语） 中文已有明确主语 卢沟桥。这句中文铺了三个动词性成分（位于、横跨、是），但最核心、定性的 是判断句「是…多拱石桥」，所以主干定成 Lugou Bridge is the oldest multi-arch stone bridge，主语 Lugou Bridge、系动词 is、表语 the oldest multi-arch stone bridge。「位于」 和「横跨」只是描述位置，降级即可。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 位于、横跨降级成分词/独立分句 主干之外两块降级安放：位于天安门广场西南15公里处 处理成 located 15 kilometres southwest of Tian'anmen Square（过去分词作状语/可前置）；横跨永定河 处理成 and spans the Yongding River（用 and 接一个并列谓语，或写成 spanning the Yongding River 的现在分词后 置定语）。这样三个信息（位置、横跨、定性）就有主有从，而不是三个动词平铺。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般现在时：is/spans——这是桥现在仍成立的事实。 最高级冠词 最古老的 用最高级 the oldest，最高级前必须加定冠词 the。 方位介词 西南15公里处 译 15 kilometres southwest of…，用 southwest of 表「在…西南方」，距离 15 kilometres 置于方位词前。 复合形容词 多拱 译 multi-arch（连字符合成的前置定语），arch 用单数作定语；若用 multi-arched 亦可。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Located 15 kilometres southwest of Tian'anmen Square and spanning the Yongding River, Lugou Bridge is the oldest existing multi-arch stone bridge in Beijing. 2. 卢沟桥最初建成于1192年，1698年重建，由281根柱子支撑。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 桥 was built / rebuilt（主语策略：转被动） 中文「建成」「重建」「支撑」三个动作的承受者都是桥本身——桥是被建、被重建、被柱子支撑 的，没有主动施事者出现，故转被动，把承受者 Lugou Bridge/It 提作主语：It was first built…, rebuilt…, and is supported by 281 pillars。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 三动作并列＋柱子作工具 最初建成于1192年 与 1698年重建 是两个先后发生的过去动作，用 first built in 1192 and rebuilt in 1698 并列（共享主语）；由281根柱子支撑 是它现在的结构状态，用 is supported by 281 pillars，by 引出施事/支撑物。注意这第三块是「现在仍被支撑」，与前两块的过去动作时态 不同，不要一律塞进过去式。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 建成重建 是过去已完成动作，偏离基调用一般过去时 was built/rebuilt；由281根柱子支撑 是现在 仍成立的结构，回到基调用一般现在时被动 is supported。一句之内两种时态，要分清。 语态 三处全用被动：was built / was rebuilt / is supported by——桥是被建、被支撑的。 单复数 281根柱子 是复数 281 pillars，pillar 加 -s。 时间介词 「于1192年/1698年」用 in + 年份：in 1192, in 1698。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: It was first built in 1192 and rebuilt in 1698, and is supported by 281 pillars. 3. 每根柱子上都有一头石狮。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: There is a stone lion（主语策略：There be） 中文 每根柱子上都有一头石狮 表「某处存在某物」，是典型的存在句，用 There be 句型最自然： There is a stone lion on each pillar。主语形式上是 there，真正存在的事物 a stone lion 放在 is 之后。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 地点状语后置 本句结构简单，主干即全句，只需把 每根柱子上 处理成地点状语 on each pillar 放句末。无多余 分句需降级。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指基调用一般现在时 There is——这是桥现在的常态。 主谓一致 一头石狮 是单数，There be 的 be 跟其后名词走，故用 is，配单数 a stone lion。 单复数与冠词 一头石狮 此处确是单数（每根柱子各一头），用 a stone lion，与下文成群的 stone lions 复数区 分开。 分配词 每根柱子 用 each pillar（each 后接单数名词），呼应「每根上各有一头」的分配含义。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: On each pillar stands a stone lion. 4. 这些石狮的头、背、腹部或爪子上都藏着更多的狮子。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: more lions are hidden（主语策略：转被动） 中文「藏着更多的狮子」没有明确施事者（不是谁去藏的），重在「更多狮子被藏在某处」这一状 态，故转被动，把承受者 more lions 提作主语：More lions are hidden on the head, back, belly or paws…。也可保留 这些石狮 作主语写主动 these stone lions hide more lions，但被动 更贴「藏着」的静态含义。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 四个部位并列作地点状语 头、背、腹部或爪子 是「狮子被藏的位置」，并列成名词串作介词 on 的宾语：on the heads, backs, bellies or paws of these stone lions，用 of 短语把「这些石狮的」处理成后置所属，避 免照中文「这些石狮的头背腹爪」语序硬堆在前面。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指基调用一般现在时被动 are hidden——这是石狮现在的样貌常态。 语态 用被动 are hidden（更多狮子被藏着）。 单复数 这些石狮 复数 these stone lions；部位 heads/backs/bellies/paws 因主体是众多石狮，宜用复 数；belly 复数为 bellies（辅音 + y 变 ies）。 并列连词 头、背、腹部或爪子 用「或」对应 or 连接最后一项：heads, backs, bellies or paws。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: On the heads, backs, bellies or paws of these stone lions are hidden even more lions. 5. 这些石狮生动逼真、千姿百态，是卢沟桥石刻艺术的精品。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 石狮 are 精品（主语策略：原句主语） 中文已有明确主语 这些石狮。句中「生动逼真、千姿百态」是描述其状貌的形容性成分，「是…精 品」是判断核心，故主干定成判断句 These stone lions are the finest works…，主语 these stone lions、系动词 are、表语 the finest works of stone carving。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 形容词组降级成插入语 生动逼真、千姿百态 不照中文塞成一串谓语，而降级成插入性的形容词短语：Vivid and lifelike, varying in posture, these stone lions are…（前置形容词状语），或用定语从句 which are vivid and lifelike。这样主干「是精品」清晰，描写作修饰挂在前面。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指基调用一般现在时 are——石狮当下的特征与艺术地位。 主谓一致 这些石狮 复数 these stone lions，系动词用 are，表语 the finest works 也用复数呼应。 四字词意译 生动逼真 译 vivid and lifelike；千姿百态 不可逐字译，意译为 varying in posture/in a variety of postures，抓「姿态多样」之意。 用词搭配 精品 译 the finest works/masterpieces；石刻艺术 译 the stone carving art/the art of stone carving。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Vivid and lifelike, varying in posture, these stone lions are regarded as the finest works of stone carving on Lugou Bridge. 6. 桥上的石狮不计其数，因而北京地区流传着"卢沟桥上的石狮子——数不清"的说法。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 石狮 are countless 引出谚语（主语策略：原句主语） 中文是「原因（石狮不计其数） 结果（流传着…说法）」的因果句。前半 桥上的石狮不计其数 以 stone lions 为主语：The stone lions on the bridge are countless/too many to count；后 半 北京地区流传着…的说法 表「某说法被流传」，可转被动 a saying… is popular/has spread， 或用 there be。两个分句用 so/thus 显因果。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 谚语直引＋说法转被动 卢沟桥上的石狮子——数不清 是一句民间谚语，作 saying 的内容，用引号直引并意 译：the saying "The stone lions on Lugou Bridge are countless"。北京地区流传着… 说法 转被动/存在：there is a popular saying in Beijing that…，把「流传着」处理成 popular/widely circulated。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指基调用一般现在时：are countless/there is a saying——这是至今仍成立的事实与仍在流传 的说法。 因果连词 因而 用 so/thus/therefore 显化因果，不要只用逗号粘连两个独立句（避免 comma splice 病 句）。 单复数 桥上的石狮 复数 the stone lions；谚语内 lions 亦复数。 用词 不计其数 译 countless/too numerous to count/innumerable；数不清 谚语收尾的「数不清」对 应 too many to count/impossible to count。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The stone lions on the bridge are too numerous to count, so there is a popular saying in the Beijing area: "The stone lions on Lugou Bridge are simply countless." 7. 卢沟桥不仅以其美学特征闻名于世，还被公认为石桥建筑史上的一座丰碑。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 卢沟桥 is famous … and is recognized as 丰碑（主语策略：原句主语） 中文已有明确主语 卢沟桥。句子是「不仅A，还B」的递进并列：A=以其美学特征闻名于世 → is famous for its aesthetic features；B=被公认为…丰碑 → is recognized as a monument。主干 即 Lugou Bridge is not only famous… but also recognized as…，两个表语并列。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 两个并列表语共享主语 本句无需复杂降级，关键是 not only…but also… 把两个并列谓语/表语挂到同一主语上：is not only famous for its aesthetic features but also recognized as a monument…，避免写成两个 独立的 It is famous… It is recognized… 散句。「石桥建筑史上」作 monument 的后置定语 in the history of stone bridge construction。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指基调用一般现在时 is famous/is recognized——其声誉与地位至今成立。 语态 被公认为 用被动 is recognized as/is acknowledged as。 介词搭配 闻名于世 用 be famous for（因…而闻名）+ its aesthetic features；被公认为 用 be recognized/regarded as + 名词。for 与 as 不可混用。 冠词 一座丰碑 是泛指「一座」，用不定冠词 a monument/a landmark。
